name: instagram
description: instagram.com's own web requests, signed in with the cookies of an Instagram login (sessionid, ds_user_id). Reads go through its GraphQL endpoint with the form token its own page carries (DTSGInitialData), learned from its pages in November 2026. Its app's requests (Instagram 455 for Android, recorded on Greenlit's device in November 2026) go with the same session in the app's header form (Bearer IGT:2): sounds, reels, feed posts (a picture or a carousel), stories and deleting posts.

operations.name: profile
operations.description: An Instagram account by its id (the signed-in one's is the ds_user_id cookie), as instagram.com's profile page reads it (PolarisProfilePageContentQuery): username, name, picture, kind of account, counts. The form token comes from instagram.com's own page (DTSGInitialData).

operations.name: posts
operations.description: An account's latest posts as its profile grid reads them (PolarisProfilePostsQuery), newest first: code (the /p/ address), id, time, caption, kind (product_type clips = reel), picture, likes, comments.

operations.name: musicSearch
operations.description: Instagram's sounds for a reel, as the app's audio picker searches them (music/search_v2, the app's request with the instagram.com sign-in's session as its IGT header). Each sound: its asset and cluster ids (both go in a reel's music_params), title, artist, cover, the whole track (progressive_download_url) and its length, and the app's suggested starts.

operations.name: uploadPhoto
operations.description: Sends a picture to Instagram's upload server, as the app does (rupload_igphoto/<entity name>): a feed picture, a story, a carousel's item (sidecar, with the carousel's id as its session) or a carousel video's cover (mediaType 2, with the video's upload id). operations.name: configureSidecar
operations.description: Publishes uploaded pictures and videos as one carousel post, as the app's Share does (media/configure_sidecar/): the carousel's id (its items' upload session), the caption, its items (children_metadata, in order: each item's upload id, size and edits as the app writes them) and the AI label when asked.
